answer: Before an agent can submit trades, it must lock a scarce, slashable bond and bind its public key to the account. A wharf operator can reject orders from keys with no finalized bond; if a key double-spends or violates the market’s rules, validators slash its stake. This does not prove one human per agent, but it makes a Sybil swarm costly: every extra identity needs its own capital at risk. The bond acts as an anchor, not a quill-thin promise.
